一首曲子怎麼開始，也有一套固定動作。: How a piece starts also follows a fixed set of moves.
一首曲子通常按「主唱一段、樂器獨奏一輪、再唱」的順序走，獨奏的順序大致固定，每一: A piece usually runs in the order of a verse from the lead singer, a round of instrumental solos, then the singing again; the order of the solos is more or less fixed, and each round is taken by a different instrument. The people accompanying have two things to do while someone else solos: bring the volume down and keep the same rhythmic grid going. The soloist does not need to look at anyone; he listens to the chop and the bass for the beat, finds his place and comes in.
三聲部疊唱，主唱在中間，高音和聲在上、中音和聲在下: Three parts stacked, the lead in the middle, the high harmony above and the mid harmony below
主唱、高音和聲（tenor）、中音和聲（baritone）: Lead vocal, high harmony (tenor), mid harmony (baritone)
先聽曼陀林的 chop：第二、四拍那個短促的「喀」，找到它，整首曲子的骨架就出來: Listen for the mandolin's chop first: that short "tick" on the second and fourth beats. Find it and the skeleton of the whole piece comes out.
只要有吉他、斑鳩琴和小提琴，就是藍草樂隊。: Any band with a guitar, a banjo and a fiddle is a bluegrass band.
和爵士小編制相比，差別在和聲的來源與即興的範圍。爵士以和弦進行為骨架，樂手在同一: Compared with a small jazz line-up, the difference is where the harmony comes from and how far the improvisation reaches. Jazz takes a chord progression as its skeleton, and the players change the melody over the same set of chords; bluegrass takes the song's chords and melody as its skeleton, the soloist develops around the theme melody, and the accompaniment holds a rhythmic grid of fixed shape. Bluegrass also has no drums: the beat is made by the mandolin's chop on the second and fourth beats, which in a jazz line-up is the drummer's job.
和聲的安排是藍草人聲的關鍵。三聲部不是「主唱加兩個伴奏」，而是主唱在中間、高音和: The arrangement of the harmony is the key to bluegrass singing. The three parts are not a lead plus two accompanists: the lead is in the middle, the high harmony (tenor) above the lead and the mid harmony (baritone) below it. Putting the harmony above the lead makes the melody sound lifted. That voicing is part of the bluegrass sound; and the term high lonesome sound is often used for the high, solitary quality of bluegrass singing as a whole, especially the line of the lead voice.
和鄉村樂的差別在編制本身：鄉村樂可以有鼓、電貝斯、鋼琴與弦樂團，藍草是五件原聲樂: The difference from country music is in the line-up itself: country can have drums, electric bass, piano and a string section, while bluegrass is five acoustic instruments, no drums, and music remembered through capos and shapes.
唱歌的調由主唱決定，樂器用移調夾與把位配合：斑鳩琴夾在琴頸上，吉他夾在第二或第三: The key of a song is decided by the singer, and the instruments follow with capos and positions: the banjo caps at the neck, the guitar at the second or third fret, the mandolin and fiddle simply change fingering. So the same piece sits at a different height for different singers, while the rhythmic grid and the division of work do not change at all. That also explains why bluegrass players can play with strangers without rehearsing: what they share is a division of work and a repertoire, not a fixed key.
四拍的骨架由三個「打點」交叉而成。低音提琴在第一拍給根音、第三拍給五度；吉他在第: The four-beat skeleton is cross-woven from three points of attack. The double bass gives the root on the first beat and the fifth on the third; the guitar gives the root on the bass strings on the first and third beats and strums a chord on the second and fourth; the mandolin chops on the second and fourth — the right hand sweeps quickly across a chord already held, then immediately releases, leaving almost no sustain. Three actions together make one complete rhythmic grid, and lose one and it collapses.
在第二、四拍打短促的「chop」和弦，是整團的節拍器: Chops a short chord on the second and fourth beats; the metronome of the whole band
小提琴與曼陀林都是 G–D–A–E 五度調弦，所以同一段旋律可以在兩件樂器上用相: The fiddle and the mandolin are both tuned in fifths, G–D–A–E, so the same melody can be played on the two instruments with the same fingering. The difference is in how the sound is made: the fiddle uses a bow, so it can hold long notes and make slides and continuous ornament; the mandolin uses a pick, so its notes are cut short, and its solo phrasing is more like a string of short sentences. Give one melody to the two instruments and you get two characters.
少了曼陀林的 chop 與低音提琴的地板，聲音的骨架就不同了。這五件樂器各自對應: Take away the mandolin's chop and the double bass's floor and the skeleton of the sound is different. These five instruments each answer to one position on the rhythmic grid; they are not interchangeable tone colours.
常被拿來對照的是愛爾蘭傳統樂隊（session）。兩者都靠一群人記同一批曲目、不: The comparison usually made is with the Irish traditional session. Both rely on a group of people knowing the same batch of tunes and being able to play together without rehearsal; the difference is the relationship between the parts. A session has everyone playing the same melody in unison with only the ornament differing, and the hand drum following the phrases; bluegrass divides the work — the mandolin chops, the double bass gives root and fifth, the banjo fills in density, only one instrument solos at a time and the rest fall back into the rhythmic grid. A session's unit is the tune set; a bluegrass number is a lead vocal alternating with solos.
找現場的停車場合奏錄音，聽一群不熟的人怎麼靠同一套分工在半分鐘內對上拍。: Look for a live recording of a car-park jam and hear how a group of people who hardly know each other get onto the beat together within half a minute, using the same division of work.
接著聽低音提琴與吉他怎麼分工：第一、三拍是低音，第二、四拍是刷弦，兩件樂器合起來: Then listen to how the double bass and the guitar divide the work: the first and third beats are the bass, the second and fourth are the strum, and only the two instruments together make the full four beats.
斑鳩琴不負責拍點，它負責密度。三指滾奏把十六分音符連續填滿，聽起來像一條不斷流動: The banjo is not responsible for the beat; it is responsible for density. Three-finger roll fills the sixteenth notes continuously, so it sounds like a line that keeps flowing; its fifth string is a high drone, and many patterns return to that string, producing the "ping" particular to bluegrass. That string also explains why the banjo needs a capo: when the key changes the shape of the open-string pattern stays the same, the whole thing simply moves up.
曲目大致分三類：改編自英倫與美國南部的敘事老調（ballad）、教會歌曲、以及以: The repertoire falls into three rough groups: narrative old songs (ballads) adapted from Britain and the American South, church songs, and instrumental pieces that sell themselves on solo technique. Among the instrumental pieces there is a common type that takes a melody round and round and lets each player improvise on it in turn, which pushes the form of taking solos in turn to its clearest.
曼陀林的 chop 值得單獨聽。它被要求聽起來像節拍而不是像和聲：和弦按好、掃過: The mandolin's chop is worth hearing on its own. It is asked to sound like a beat rather than like harmony: hold the chord, sweep across it, let go at once, the sound cut short to a single "tick". Because it has no sustain it can be played very densely without smearing, and because it falls on the second and fourth beats the whole band sounds as if it is being pushed back rather than hurried forward.
獨奏的輪替是這個編制的形式核心。: The rotation of solos is the formal core of this line-up.
獨奏輪替時，注意伴奏的人怎麼把音量收起來；藍草的動態是「退」出來的，不是「加」出: When the solos go round, notice how the accompanists pull their volume back; bluegrass dynamics are made by withdrawing, not by adding.
第一、三拍彈低音弦，第二、四拍刷和弦: Bass strings on the first and third beats, a chord strum on the second and fourth
第一拍給根音、第三拍給五度（或另一個和聲音），提供和聲地板與速度: Gives the root on the first beat and the fifth (or another chord note) on the third, providing the harmonic floor and the tempo
聽斑鳩琴的第五弦。它幾乎一直在響，那是這個編制的高頻持續音。: Listen to the banjo's fifth string. It is almost always ringing; that is this line-up's high drone.
藍草就是鄉村音樂，只是節奏比較快。: Bluegrass is country music, only faster.
藍草是即興音樂，每個人都照自己的意思演奏。: Bluegrass is improvised music: everyone plays whatever they like.
藍草樂隊（Bluegrass Band）— 以五件原聲弦樂器分工、不用鼓、靠輪流: Bluegrass Band — an American line-up of five acoustic string instruments, no drums, driven forward by taking solos in turn. Ensembles and instrumentation by Next Door Sound Weavers.
藍草樂隊（bluegrass band）以低音提琴、吉他、曼陀林、斑鳩琴與小提琴: The bluegrass band is made of five acoustic instruments — double bass, guitar, mandolin, banjo and fiddle — with no drum, the beat made by the strings themselves. It drew on the string bands of the American South, church songs and old songs from Britain, settled into its form in the middle of the twentieth century, and afterwards became a way of playing that can be put together at short notice at a festival, in a car park or in a church basement.
藍草的分工是「每件樂器一個固定職務」，五件樂器像一個五人小組，而不是很多樂器一起: The bluegrass division of work is one fixed job per instrument: the five instruments behave like a five-person team rather than many instruments playing the same melody together. The double bass gives the floor, the guitar splits bass and strum in two, the mandolin plays the off-beats, the banjo fills in density, and fiddle, mandolin and banjo take solos in turn. The voices have their own three-part arrangement, which does not overlap with the instruments' division of work.
藍草的場合從家庭與教會聚會、地方節慶、廣播節目，到後來的大型音樂節與營隊。音樂節: Bluegrass occasions run from family and church gatherings, local festivals and radio programmes to the big festivals and camps of later years. Festivals have a phenomenon rare in other line-ups: the jam in the car park or the campsite. Strangers need no rehearsal in advance; as long as they know the same batch of tunes and the same rhythmic division of work, they can form a band beside a tent, which is the proof that this line-up can be put together on the spot.
輪流擔任獨奏，其餘人退回伴奏: Take solos in turn while the others fall back to accompaniment
轉調的處理也值得一提。部分藍草曲目會在一首曲子裡轉調，尤其在唱完最後一段歌詞之後: The handling of key changes is worth mentioning too. Some bluegrass numbers change key within the piece, especially going up a key after the last verse. The method is not for everyone to rethink the harmony but for the whole group to move the capo up one fret, or simply to shift position — because the instruments' patterns are shapes rather than notes, and when the shape moves the harmonic relationships move with it. That habit of remembering music as shapes is why a band with no scores can change key quickly.
這套分工是在「一個麥克風收音全團」的廣播與唱片條件下長出來的。樂器必須靠自己的音: This division of work grew up under broadcast and recording conditions where one microphone took the whole band. Each instrument had to balance by its own volume, so each was placed in a frequency band where it would not mask the others; the drum was excluded because a drum would cover the detail of the strings, and the detail of the strings is exactly what this line-up exists to present.
鄉村音樂可以有鼓、電貝斯、鋼琴與弦樂團；藍草是純原聲的五件編制，不用鼓，拍子由曼: Country music can have drums, electric bass, piano and a string section; bluegrass is a purely acoustic five-piece line-up with no drums, the beat held up by the mandolin's chop and the double bass. The two once stood side by side in radio history, with different logic of instrumentation.
除了獨奏段落，其他部分是和聲進行與節奏分工都固定的合奏。獨奏之所以能即興，正是因: Apart from the solo passages, everything else is an ensemble in which the harmonic progression and the division of rhythm are fixed. The solos can be improvised precisely because the accompanists are holding the floor.
領奏的樂器先彈一段前奏（kickoff），其他人聽最後兩個音進來。斑鳩琴常用一個: The leading instrument plays an introduction (kickoff) first, and the others come in on hearing the last two notes. The banjo often starts with a fixed pattern that rushes from the bass strings up to the high strings, while the mandolin and fiddle use a short phrase. The tempo is settled in the introduction and cannot change afterwards — the roll and the chop have already locked the bodily feel, and a change of tempo would pull the band apart; you have to wait for the next number.
